notes: Adversaries as printed in the SRD. Numbers here match the book exactly - per-encounter tuning belongs in encounters/, so these stay checkable against the printed page. Entries are in the book's own tier-then-print order, and PORTED.md tracks which of the SRD's 129 are in and which are still out. Every entry states the damage_type printed beside its standard attack; the field accepts the book's own 'phy' and 'mag' too, and an entry that omitted it would simply never have anyone's resistance applied to it.

adversaries.name: Acid Burrower
adversaries.notes: Claws: Very Close, 1d12+2 physical. Experience: Tremor Sense +2.

adversaries.name: Bear
adversaries.notes: Claws: Melee, 1d8+3 physical. Experience: Ambusher +3, Keen Senses +2.

adversaries.name: Cave Ogre
adversaries.notes: Club: Very Close, 1d10+2 physical. Experience: Throw +2.

adversaries.name: Construct
adversaries.notes: Fist Slam: Melee, 1d20 physical - the one tier 1 standard attack with no flat bonus. No Experience printed. Weak Structure worsens physical damage only, which the code now enforces; Death Quake's blast is magic and is typed where the feature rolls it.

adversaries.name: Deeproot Defender
adversaries.notes: Vines: Close, 1d8+3 physical. Experience: Huge +3.

adversaries.name: Dire Wolf
adversaries.notes: Claws: Melee, 1d6+2 physical. Experience: Keen Senses +3. Pack Tactics carries two terms because the SRD prints it differently on the two stat blocks that have it: the Wolf's deals 1d6+5 *and pays the GM a Fear*, where the Sylvan Soldier's deals 1d8+5 and pays nothing. Both halves are authored here rather than in code, so the entry stays checkable against the page.

adversaries.name: Giant Mosquitoes
adversaries.notes: Proboscis: Melee, 1d8+3 physical. Experience: Camouflage +2. The type reads 'Horde (5/HP)' on the page - that is the Battle Points shorthand, not the feature's number, which is the 1d4+1 in the feature name.

adversaries.name: Giant Rat
adversaries.notes: Claws: Melee, a flat 1 physical - no dice at all, which is why damage_dice is empty and the whole attack sits in damage_modifier. Thresholds print as 'None'; a Minion is defeated by any damage, so there is no second HP for a threshold to matter for. Experience: Keen Senses +3.

adversaries.name: Giant Scorpion
adversaries.notes: Pincers: Melee, 1d12+2 physical. Experience: Camouflage +2. Momentum is the same feature the Bear carries and is already modelled.

adversaries.name: Glass Snake
adversaries.notes: Glass Fangs: Very Close, 1d8+2 physical. No Experience printed.

adversaries.name: Harrier
adversaries.notes: Javelin: Close, 1d6+2 physical. Experience: Camouflage +2. Fall Back is the first Reaction that interrupts an incoming attack rather than responding to one that landed.

adversaries.name: Archer Guard
adversaries.notes: Longbow: Far, 1d8+3 physical. Experience: Local Knowledge +3. Three HP against two Stress means the Stress-desperation rule never holds Hobbling Shot back - the Archer is always inside the line.

adversaries.name: Bladed Guard
adversaries.notes: Longsword: Melee, 1d6+1 physical. Experience: Local Knowledge +3.

adversaries.name: Head Guard
adversaries.notes: Mace: Melee, 1d10+4 physical. Experience: Commander +2, Local Knowledge +2. The first Leader ported - type carries no mechanics, so nothing in the loop reads it. The book prints the second feature as 'On My Signal - Reaction: Countdown (5)'; the 5 is the countdown's starting value and is carried as the feature's parameter, the way Flying (X) and Horde (X) carry theirs. Momentum is already modelled for the Bear.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Bandit
adversaries.notes: Daggers: Melee, 1d8+1 physical. Experience: Thief +2.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Hexer
adversaries.notes: Staff: Far, 1d6+2 magic. Experience: Magical Knowledge +2. One of the two tier 1 stat blocks whose standard attack is magic, so it is the one a resistant target actually notices. Chaotic Flux is magic too and is typed where the feature rolls it.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Kneebreaker
adversaries.notes: Club: Melee, 1d4+6 physical. Experience: Thief +2, Unveiled Threats +3. The apostrophes in the first feature name are straight ones: canonical matching folds case and whitespace but deliberately not punctuation, so a typographic apostrophe here would silently never reach the code. Both features are built on Restrained, which is ruled to have no combat effect - see PORTED.md for what is left of them.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Lackey
adversaries.notes: Daggers: Melee, a flat 2 physical - no dice at all, so damage_dice is empty and the whole attack sits in damage_modifier, exactly as the Giant Rat's does. Thresholds print as 'None'. Experience: Thief +2. Both features are already modelled and needed no new code: Minion (X) reads its own number off this stat block, and Group Attack was deliberately written for Minions in general rather than for the Giant Rat.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Lieutenant
adversaries.notes: Javelin: Close, 1d8+3 physical. Experience: Local Knowledge +2. More Where That Came From summons three Jagged Knife Lackeys, so this entry is only complete because that stat block is in the catalogue too. Momentum is already modelled.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Shadow
adversaries.notes: Daggers: Melee, 1d4+4 physical. Experience: Intrusion +3. Both features turn on an adversary attacking with Advantage, which in this simulator has exactly one source today - the target being Vulnerable.

adversaries.name: Jagged Knife Sniper
adversaries.notes: Shortbow: Far, 1d10+2 physical.

adversaries.name: Minor Chaos Elemental
adversaries.notes: Warp Blast: Close, 1d12+6 magic. No Experience printed. Arcane Form makes this the first adversary in the catalogue that is resistant to a damage type, so a party's weapon choices start to matter against it. Sickening Flux is the first feature whose cost is the adversary's own HP rather than Stress or Fear, and Magical Reflection the first that needs to know both who attacked and how hard. Momentum is already modelled.

adversaries.name: Minor Fire Elemental
adversaries.notes: Elemental Blast: Far, 1d10+4 magic. No Experience printed. The largest tier 1 HP track so far at 9, and a Far standard attack, so the area rule rarely holds it back. Relentless (2) and Momentum are already modelled. Scorched Earth is the first feature where a successful Reaction Roll buys half damage rather than nothing.

adversaries.name: Minor Demon
adversaries.notes: Claws: Melee, 1d8+6 physical. No Experience printed. Relentless (2) and Momentum are already modelled. Reaper scales with the Demon's own wounds, so this stat block gets more dangerous exactly as the party wears it down - the opposite of the Horde's shape.

adversaries.name: Minor Treant
adversaries.notes: Clawed Branch: Melee, a flat 4 physical - no dice, so damage_dice is empty and the whole attack sits in damage_modifier, as the Giant Rat's and Jagged Knife Lackey's do. Thresholds print as 'None'. This entry needed no new code at all: Minion (X) reads its own 5 off this stat block and Group Attack was written for Minions in general, so the whole adversary came online with its JSON. A flat 4 apiece makes a Treant Group Attack the hardest-hitting swarm in tier 1.

adversaries.name: Green Ooze
adversaries.notes: Ooze Appendage: Melee, 1d6+1 magic. Experience: Camouflage +3. Difficulty 8 is the lowest in the catalogue and is checked against the printed page - the Tiny Green Ooze it splits into is *harder* to hit at 14, which looks inverted but is what the book prints. Slow is the first feature that spends an activation without acting, and Split the first that takes an adversary off the field without defeating it. Split carries what it becomes as a parameter, the way Flying (X) carries its bonus: the book prints the name bare on both Oozes, but the Red one splits into something else.

adversaries.name: Tiny Green Ooze
adversaries.notes: Ooze Appendage: Melee, 1d4+1 magic. No Experience printed. The first entry with a *mixed* threshold - the page prints '4/None', so a Major hit marks 2 HP off a 2 HP track and nothing can reach Severe. Difficulty 14 against the Green Ooze's 8 is what the book prints, checked against the page. Two of these are what a Green Ooze becomes when it Splits, so the catalogue needs both for that feature to work.

adversaries.name: Red Ooze
adversaries.notes: Ooze Appendage: Melee, 1d8+3 magic. Experience: Camouflage +3. The Green Ooze's sibling and a straightforwardly nastier one - no Slow holding it back, and a burn that keeps costing after the hit. Split is the same feature the Green Ooze carries, told by its parameter what to become.

adversaries.name: Tiny Red Ooze
adversaries.notes: Ooze Appendage: Melee, 1d4+2 magic. No Experience printed. A mixed threshold again, '5/None'. Note it does *not* carry Acidic Form, unlike the Tiny Green Ooze - its whole defence is Burning, which taxes anybody killing it in melee. Two of these are what a Red Ooze becomes when it Splits.

adversaries.name: Pirate Captain
adversaries.notes: Cutlass: Melee, 1d12+2 physical. Experience: Commander +2, Sailor +3. Five Stress is the deepest track in tier 1. Momentum is already modelled. No Quarter needs three Pirates in Melee range of one target, which the area rule only allows on a field of six or more - so it is dead in a small crew by the printed number, not by any threshold of ours.

adversaries.name: Pirate Raiders
adversaries.notes: Cutlass: Melee, 1d8+2 physical. Experience: Sailor +3. Needed no new code beyond Swashbuckler: Horde (X) reads its own 1d4+1 off this stat block, exactly as the Giant Mosquitoes' does. The type reads 'Horde (3/HP)' on the page - that is the Battle Points shorthand, not the feature's number.

adversaries.name: Pirate Tough
adversaries.notes: Massive Fists: Melee, 2d6 physical - no flat bonus, the second tier 1 attack written that way after the Construct's. Experience: Sailor +2. Clear the Decks is worth barely more than the printed attack once its repositioning is stripped out, which is declared where it is registered.

adversaries.name: Sellsword
adversaries.notes: Longsword: Melee, a flat 3 physical - no dice, so the whole attack sits in damage_modifier, as the Giant Rat's, the Jagged Knife Lackey's and the Minor Treant's do. Thresholds print as 'None'. No Experience printed. The third stat block to come online with its JSON alone: Minion (X) reads its own 4 here and Group Attack was written for Minions in general. ATK +3 is the highest attack modifier on any tier 1 Minion, which is what makes a Sellsword Group Attack land where a Dredge's misses.

adversaries.name: Skeleton Archer
adversaries.notes: Shortbow: Far, 1d8+1 physical. No Experience printed. Difficulty 9 is the second-lowest in the catalogue after the Green Ooze's 8 - a fragile skeleton that shoots from the back. Both features want the rest of the field: Opportunist needs adversaries crowding the target, and Deadly Shot needs somebody already Vulnerable, which nothing in the Archer's own kit provides.

adversaries.name: Skeleton Dredge
adversaries.notes: Bone Claws: Melee, a flat 1 physical. Thresholds print as 'None'. No Experience printed. The same shape as the Sellsword and needed no code either, but the far weaker half of the pair: Difficulty 8 ties the Green Ooze for the easiest thing in the catalogue to hit, ATK -1 means it mostly misses, and a flat 1 apiece makes a Dredge Group Attack the feeblest swarm in tier 1. What it is really for is Opportunist - a crowd of Dredges is what doubles a Skeleton Archer's damage.

adversaries.name: Skeleton Knight
adversaries.notes: Rusty Greatsword: Melee, 1d10+2 physical. No Experience printed. The first stat block whose passive drains Hope off every landed attack, and the first that attacks back as it dies. Two Stress against 5 HP means Cut to the Bone waits until the Knight is at 5 unmarked HP - which is full health - so it is available from the opening spotlight and gone after two uses.

adversaries.name: Skeleton Warrior
adversaries.notes: Sword: Melee, 1d6+2 physical. No Experience printed. The first physical resistance in the catalogue, where Arcane Form was the first magical one. Halving lands before the Warrior's thresholds of 4 and 8, so 9 physical marks 2 HP where 9 magic marks 3 - what that comes to across a fight is for a run to say rather than for this note. Won't Stay Dead is the only feature in the catalogue that can bring an adversary back after it is defeated.

adversaries.name: Spellblade
adversaries.notes: Empowered Longsword: Melee, 1d8+4 phy/mag. Experience: Magical Knowledge +2. The first entry whose damage_type is the *pair* - the page prints 'phy/mag' beside the attack and Arcane Steel says the same thing in words, so the feature and the field agree. Ruled: such a hit is resisted if the target resists either type. Momentum is already modelled. Suppressing Blast is typed magic where it is rolled, so Arcane Steel does not reach it.

adversaries.name: Swarm of Rats
adversaries.notes: Claws: Melee, 1d8+2 physical. No Experience printed. ATK -3 is the worst attack modifier in the catalogue, so what the Swarm is really for is In Your Face rather than its own damage. Horde (X) reads its own 1d4+1 here, as the Giant Mosquitoes' and the Pirate Raiders' do. The type's '10/HP' is the Battle Points shorthand and carries no mechanics.

adversaries.name: Sylvan Soldier
adversaries.notes: Scythe: Melee, 1d8+1 physical. Experience: Tracker +2. Pack Tactics is the Dire Wolf's feature with a different argument and no Fear clause - see the Dire Wolf's entry. Forest Control prints its own Reaction Roll Difficulty of 15, four above the Soldier's own 11, which is one of the few in the catalogue not to fall back on the stat block. Blend In is what made Hidden a modelled condition.

adversaries.name: Tangle Bramble Swarm
adversaries.notes: Thorns: Melee, 1d6+3 physical. Experience: Camouflage +2. Encumber's bramble tokens are the first tokens the simulator puts on a *PC* rather than on an adversary, and the first escape roll whose Difficulty rises with what is being escaped (12 + the token count). Note the printed hp_max of 6 is only what a Swarm spawned from an encounter starts with: one produced by the Tangle Bramble's Drain and Multiply overrides it with the number of Minions combined.

adversaries.name: Tangle Bramble
adversaries.notes: Thorns: Melee, a flat 2 physical - no dice, as the Giant Rat's, the Jagged Knife Lackey's, the Minor Treant's and the Sellsword's are. Thresholds print as 'None'. No Experience printed. Unlike every Minion before it this one needed code: Drain and Multiply turns three or more of them into a Tangle Bramble Swarm Horde whose HP is the number combined, which is the first content that merges adversaries rather than splitting or summoning them.

adversaries.name: Weaponmaster
adversaries.notes: Claymore: Very Close, 1d12+2 physical. No Experience printed. Momentum is already modelled. Goading Strike is the first content that reaches the *party's* targeting rule - a Taunted PC's target is fixed to the Weaponmaster until they land a hit, which is the user's ruling on a clause the page gives two different durations for. Adrenaline Burst is the first once-per-scene heal on the GM's side.

adversaries.name: Young Dryad
adversaries.notes: Scythe: Melee, 1d8+5 physical - the largest flat bonus on any tier 1 standard attack. Experience: Leadership +3. Momentum is already modelled. Voice of the Forest is the only feature in the catalogue whose extra spotlights are free: they cost the GM no Fear and sit outside the party size + 1 cap, ruled for this feature alone. What the allies pay for them is half damage on that activation.

adversaries.name: Brawny Zombie
adversaries.notes: Slam: Very Close, 1d12+3 physical. Experience: Collateral Damage +2, Throw +4. Slow is the Green Ooze's feature, generic and needing no new code. The other two are a sequence: Rip and Tear holds somebody on a landed standard attack, and Rend Asunder is the only thing that can then use the hold. Difficulty 10 is low for a Bruiser, which is the trade the page makes for a 1d12+3 attack on a 7 HP track.

adversaries.name: Patchwork Zombie Hulk
adversaries.notes: Too Many Arms: Very Close, 1d20 physical - no flat bonus, the third tier 1 attack written that way after the Construct's and the Pirate Tough's, and the second 1d20. Experience: Intimidation +2, Tear Things Apart +2. 10 HP is the deepest track in tier 1. Destructible cuts against that: every Major or greater hit marks an extra HP, which is the Construct's Weak Structure keyed on the damage rolled instead of the mark, and with no damage-type restriction. Tormented Screams prints 'you gain a Fear for each', the phrase that settled the Skeleton Knight's Terrifying at one.

adversaries.name: Rotted Zombie
adversaries.notes: Bite: Melee, a flat 2 physical - no dice, as the Giant Rat's, the Jagged Knife Lackey's, the Minor Treant's, the Sellsword's and the Tangle Bramble's are. Thresholds print as 'None'. No Experience printed. The fourth stat block to come online with its JSON alone: Minion (X) reads its own 3 here and Group Attack was written for Minions in general. ATK -3 ties the Swarm of Rats for the worst attack modifier in the catalogue.

adversaries.name: Shambling Zombie
adversaries.notes: Bite: Melee, 1d6+1 physical. No Experience printed. Thresholds of 4/6 are the tightest gap in tier 1 - only 2 apart - so almost any real hit reaches Severe. Too Many to Handle is the first feature that hands Advantage to attacks made by somebody else, and it counts any adversary with 'Zombie' in its name, on the same reading No Quarter takes of 'three or more Pirates'.

adversaries.name: Zombie Pack
adversaries.notes: Bite: Melee, 1d10+2 physical. No Experience printed. Horde (X) reads its own 1d4+2 here, as the Giant Mosquitoes', the Pirate Raiders', the Swarm of Rats' and the Tangle Bramble Swarm's do. Overwhelm is the counterattack shape the Harrier's Fall Back has, keyed on being wounded rather than on somebody closing in - and it swings the printed attack, so a worn-down Pack hits back with the Horde damage instead. The type's '2/HP' is the Battle Points shorthand and carries no mechanics.
